examples.name: document-skeleton
examples.description: The top-level node of every template document. Exactly one root exists per document (doc.root points at it) — it is created with the document, never inserted manually. Its single "children" slot holds the document body in render order.

examples.name: minimal
examples.description: Plain paragraph with literal text content.

examples.name: with-expression
examples.description: Text with an inline data expression — references a field on the input data via {{ ... }}.

examples.name: heading
examples.description: A level-1 heading. Use the heading node type within content for h1..h6.

examples.name: minimal
examples.description: Renders the rich-text value bound at the given data path as block content (paragraphs, lists, marks).

examples.name: with-children
examples.description: Container holding a heading followed by a paragraph — typical for grouping a section.

examples.name: styled-box
examples.description: Container used purely as a styled box — bordered + padded with no children.

examples.name: two-equal
examples.description: A 50/50 split — two equal-width columns, no gap.

examples.name: one-third-two-thirds
examples.description: A 1/3 + 2/3 split with a 12pt gap. columnSizes are flex weights, not absolute widths.

examples.name: 2x2-with-header
examples.description: A 2x2 table with the first row as a header. Cells live in slots named cell-<row>-<col>.

examples.name: invoice-line-items
examples.description: Iterate over an "items" array and render one row per item, with description / quantity / amount columns. Each datatable-column owns a body slot whose children are evaluated once per iteration with the item alias in scope.

examples.name: minimal
examples.description: A single datatable-column with a literal header and an empty body slot. Standalone fragment — embed inside a datatable's "columns" slot for it to render.

examples.name: data-bound-link
examples.description: QR code whose value is taken from a data field — e.g. a payment URL. The value prop is an expression, not a literal string.

examples.name: static-string
examples.description: QR code with a literal value. Use a JSONata string literal (single quotes) inside the raw expression.

examples.name: empty
examples.description: A placeholder with no default content. Both slots empty — the simplest authoring shape.

examples.name: with-default
examples.description: A placeholder with a default text node in the `default` slot. Templates that do not fill the placeholder show this fallback. The `fill` slot starts empty.

examples.name: show-when-present
examples.description: Render the body only when the data field exists. Uses the JSONata $exists() helper.

examples.name: inverse-else
examples.description: Inverted condition — body renders only when the expression is FALSEY. Useful as the "else" branch.

examples.name: over-array
examples.description: Iterate over an array on the input data. Each iteration introduces "item" as a scoped variable referenceable inside the body slot.

examples.name: bulleted-list
examples.description: Render an array as a bulleted list. The item-template slot holds one example item; the list expands at render time.

examples.name: numbered-list
examples.description: Same as bulleted-list but using a decimal (1., 2., 3.) marker via listType="decimal".

examples.name: styled-bullet-list
examples.description: A bulleted list with a non-default marker glyph via bulletStyle. Mirrors the Text component's bullet styles (disc, circle, square, dash); the same glyph renders whether the list is typed in a Text block or generated by a datalist. Note: circle/square only render with an embedding font — disc and dash are safe in standard PDFs.

examples.name: thin-line
examples.description: A 1pt solid horizontal rule, full-width — the typical visual section break.

examples.name: din-c56-left
examples.description: Standard left-window envelope address block (DIN C5/C6) with the recipient address rendered from data fields. Singleton: only one address block per document is allowed.

examples.name: minimal
examples.description: A hard page break — forces a new page in the rendered document.

examples.name: title-only
examples.description: Minimal page header with a single text block. Anchored to the top of every page. When the document declares a second pageheader the second one renders on pages 2..N and this one applies only to page 1.

examples.name: first-page-cover
examples.description: A taller first-page header for cover-page patterns.

examples.name: running-header
examples.description: A compact running header for pages after the cover page.

examples.name: centered-text
examples.description: Page footer with a single centered text block. Anchored to the bottom of every page.

examples.name: placeholder
examples.description: An empty image node with no assigned asset. The assetId is null, so the renderer shows a placeholder. Set assetId to a valid asset reference and width/height to render the actual image.

examples.name: with-asset
examples.description: An image node referencing a real asset (the Epistola logo from the demo catalog: slug 01966a00-0000-7000-8000-000000000001). The catalogKey records which catalog the asset lives in, so the reference works across catalogs. Width and height are set in points — the renderer fetches the asset binary when producing the PDF.

examples.name: with-placeholder
examples.description: A published stencil instance (as it appears inside a template) containing one placeholder named "body". The placeholder owns two slots: `default` (set by the stencil author at publish time) and `fill` (the template override; empty here, so the renderer falls back to the default). Replacing or adding to `fill` overrides the default; clearing `fill` reverts to the default.

examples.name: with-overridden-placeholder
examples.description: Same stencil as `with-placeholder`, but the template has overridden the placeholder by populating its `fill` slot. The renderer prefers `fill` over `default` when fill is non-empty, so this stencil instance renders "Custom body — overridden" instead of the default. Clearing `fill` would revert to the default.
